page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.24xlarge belongs to the high clock speed instance family, built on KVM virtualization and x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processors running at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz across 96 vCPUs. With a total of 768 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, accommodating substantial in-memory footprints while delivering high per-core execution speeds.

Hardware acceleration and integrated physical storage are absent on this profile. The instance includes 0 GPUs and provides no local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data and operating file systems depend entirely on networked block storage volumes. Network interface performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps, supporting significant data transfer rates across internal infrastructure, though it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

The combination of high CPU clock speeds and an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation positions this instance for resource-intensive, memory-bound computing. Cost efficiency centers around dense consolidation, allowing enterprises to run large enterprise software deployments without partitioning across multiple smaller instances. Tradeoffs include the operational dependency on networked storage latency and the lack of specialized hardware accelerators.

Appropriate workloads for ecs.hfr7.24xlarge include large-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation, batch financial modeling, distributed caching layers, and enterprise memory-intensive applications requiring sustained clock performance.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.24xlarge is a high clock speed, memory-optimized instance engineered for computationally intensive enterprise applications. Driven by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processors operating at 3.3 GHz, it supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 768 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced 8 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without discrete GPUs and features no onboard local disk storage, necessitating network-attached block storage for operating environments and persistence. Network throughput is anchored by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth, enabling high-volume distributed communication. The platform's dense allocation of high-frequency compute cores and broad memory space delivers strong consolidation value for large footprints, balanced against the tradeoff of full remote storage reliance. It is technically appropriate for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caches, high-throughput computational analytics, and financial risk simulations.
